description: The goal of the proposed VPA is the installation of water treatment systems to provide safe drinking water to the individual households in Yavatmal, Ahmednagar & Jalgaon districts in Maharashtra. name: VPA-1 COMMUNITY COOKSTOVE PROGRAM IN MADAGASCAR BY WEACT
description:
This is the first Real Case VPA of the GS PoA titled "COMMUNITY COOKSTOVE PROGRAM IN MADAGASCAR BY WEACT", which is proposed under Gold Standard and currently under Preliminary Review. The proposed project boundary for the VPA is Antsirabe region of Republic of Madagascar.
This VPA will involve new distribution of Improved Cookstoves to the target population where baseline is identified as inefficient cooking practices that mainly includes open firing with three stone arrangement. This VPA is proposed to be a micro scale project, thus total emission reductions to be achieved annually shall be within the limit of 10,000 tCO2e.  This VPA is proposed and to be implemented by CME, WeAct Pty Ltd., with the help of local partners. The VPA will achieve the objective of the PoA while achieving long term sustainable development in the region.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: Community Cookstove Program in Madagascar by WeAct

name: Community Cookstove Program in Madagascar by WeAct
description:
This is a Program of Activities (PoA) proposed under the Gold Standard Mechanism, an initiative promoted and to be implemented by WeAct Pty Ltd, in Madagascar.  The primary goal of this PoA is to distribute efficient improved cooking stoves (ICS) to rural households in Madagascar; also in urban & per-urban areas depending on the baseline condition and need of the community. This initiative primarily aims to reduce firewood consumption, thereby mitigating climate change in a sustainable manner while addressing to a range of sustainable development actions for the communities. 

Currently the PoA is under development stage with an identified real case VPA which is yet to be started. Therefore, this Programme and the VPAs are proposed and yet to be started or implemented.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Canbaz Shipping Group Retrofit Project 1
description:
Shipping is a major source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions globally, responsible for over 1 Gt of CO2eq in 2018, as per the International Maritime Organization's 2020 report. GHG emissions from international shipping are largely from fuel consumption in engines using fuel oil, diesel and some LNG. Energy efficiency improvements in shipping reduce fuel consumption in ships, leading to reduced CO2 emissions.

Canbaz Shipping Group (CSG) has made the decision to apply several energy efficiency retrofit measures to their fleet of ships. CSG is undertaking a Gold Standard project to apply for the issuance of carbon credits related to the retrofit energy efficiency measures installed and to-be-installed on a specific group of 6 vessels.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
methodology: GS Retrofit Energy Efficiency Measures in Shipping v2
project_developer: IO'S GEMI KIRALAMA VE DIS TIC. LTD. STI.

name: GS 12544 VPA 01 Sidama Multipurpose Cook Stove Distribution Project
description: Sidama coffee farmers cook stove distribution project is a small scale project activity that will disseminate improved cook stoves for coffee farmers in Sidama region of Ethiopia. The project will be implemented in Aleta Wondo, Dara and Dale districts. Farmers in the project area depends on open fire for cooking. This project aimed to replace the traditional open fire stove using improved cook stoves that meet the demand of the community and improve the health and economic conditions of the community and improve the climate condition of the area.  The improved cook stove has thermal efficiency of 32% and 54% fuel saving potential. The stove will reduce GHG emissions, deforestation, and improve the health condition of the farmers.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
project_developer: Addis Ababa University - Horn of Africa Regional Environmental Center and Network (AAU-HoAREC&N)
poa_project_name: Horn of Africa energy efficient technology distribution program of activity

name: GS23280 VPA-1 RANOVOLA Water Program in Madagascar
description: The RANOVOLA project, building on infrastructure put in place by other HELVETAS initiatives, aims to ensure safe and sustainable access to clean water for the most vulnerable rural communities in Madagascar. The RANOVOLA project main objectives are to provide reliable access to clean water, improve public health by reducing the prevalence of waterborne diseases, strengthen the autonomy of local communities by collaborating with private operators to manage the operation and maintenance of the established infrastructure, support the ecological transition by limiting dependence on fossil fuels and firewood for water purification, and contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by acting on health, environmental, economic, and social fronts. The RANOVOLA project infrastructure will rely on two main technologies: 1) gravitational systems, using water sources located at higher altitudes to transport water to communities without the need for additional energy; and 2) solar pumping systems, utilizing boreholes to ensure a constant and economical water supply. In both cases, water treatment is carried out by filtration, chlorination, and iron removal. The operation and management of the infrastructure will be ensured by private operators, under a decentralized management model in compliance with Malagasy legal frameworks.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Chestnut Sustainable Restoration Megaton Project
description:
The United States is home to over 700 million acres of forestland, nearly 7.5% of the world’s forests, that provide clean water, recreation, and other life-sustaining resources to Americans. The importance of American forests to the global ecosystem and climate is central to the work of CC Project SPV, LLC (“Project Developer”), a US-based company that seeks to restore and conserve functional forestland throughout the United States for the primary purpose of increasing carbon sequestration. 

Using the Gold Standard Land Use and Forest Activities Requirements and A/R (afforestation and reforestation) methodologies, the Project Developer is implementing an afforestation project called the Chestnut Sustainable Restoration Megaton Project on multiple parcels of land within the United States. The Project Developer will be acquiring and leasing unproductive, intensively managed pasture and croplands to plant trees and restore diverse, native forests. The purpose of the project is to increase carbon stocks and sequester greenhouse gases while creating sustainably managed native forestland throughout the country. The Project Developer has extensive expertise in carbon project development and forest management. The Project Developer’s employees will manage planted forests and maintain the project’s Forest Stewardship Council certification.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

sustainable_development_goals.name: Goal 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth

name: Azimayi Improved Cookstoves in the Republic of Malawi
description:
Azimayi Improved Cookstoves in the Republic of Malawi” is a large-scale project that aims to distribute energy-efficient improved cooking solutions (ICS) in domestic households and communities in the Republic of Malawi (project location), thereby replacing traditional inefficient cooking devices that utilize firewood as a primary cooking fuel in the baseline. 

Traditional cooking methods (use of inefficient, solid biomass cooking devices like 3-stone fires/ open fires and/or traditional solid fuel stoves) prevalent across the Republic of Malawi generate significant volumes of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions attributed to the inefficient combustion of unsustainably sourced, non-renewable biomass (NRB) fuel.

The project activity includes the dissemination of project ICS to beneficiaries using traditional modes of cooking in the baseline. The project ICS employs natural draft technology to improve fuel combustion, aiding better heat transfer to the cooking pots.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Nature-based Solutions for Regenerated Forests and Community Resilience in Ethiopia - Chifra 01
description:
The “Nature-based Solutions for Regenerated Forests and Community Resilience in Chifra – Afar Region” aims to regenerate and reforest an area of approximately 4,756 ha in the Chifra Woredas of Afar Regional State of Ethiopia. This project will be developed as a Voluntary Project Activity (VPA) under the Gold Standard Programme of Activities (PoA): “Nature-based Solutions for Regenerated Forests and Community Resilience in Ethiopia”. 

The project aims to restore the degraded rangelands in the Chifra Woreda by utilising Farmer-Managed Natural Regeneration (FMNR) as a primary approach, with the inclusion of enrichment planting, involving cultivating seedlings in nurseries.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: Nature-based Solutions for Regenerated Forests and Community Resilience in Ethiopia

name: Nature-based Solutions for Regenerated Forests and Community Resilience in Ethiopia
description:
World Vision Australia intends to implement this Programme of Activities (PoA) for afforestation and reforestation activities in several states of Ethiopia. 

The PoA aims to regenerate degraded land through the implementation of the Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration (FMNR) practice and enrichment planting (described in the section A.3). By sequestering carbon, the PoA contributes to climate change mitigation efforts while improving local biodiversity, soil fertility, and water retention. These interventions aim to provide long-term benefits to local communities by creating sustainable livelihoods and promoting ecosystem services.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
